title: regexp_match produces unstable cache keys when used with flags parameter

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Describe the bug

When the regexp_match function is used with the flags parameter (e.g. `regexp_flags('*', flags='i')`) then the resulting construct receives a different cache key for SQL compilation caching every time the function is called. The result is that any SQL containing the function pollutes the compilation cache without ever being reused.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.17

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

psycopg

### Database Vendor and Major Version

Postgresql 15

### Python Version

3.11

### Operating system

Linux

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import column

def make_regexp(text):
    return column('a').regexp_match(text, flags='i')

sql1 = make_regexp('foo')
sql2 = make_regexp('bar')
print(sql1._generate_cache_key())
print(sql2._generate_cache_key())
```


### Error

The output of the test program:
```
CacheKey(key=(
  '0', 
  <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.BinaryExpression'>, 
  'left', 
  (
    '1', 
    <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.ColumnClause'>, 
    'name', 
    'a', 
    'type', 
    (
      <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes.NullType'>, 
    ),
  ),
  'right', 
  (
    '2', 
    <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.BindParameter'>, 
    (
      <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes.String'>, 
    ),
    '3', 
    False, 
  ),
  'operator', 
  <function regexp_match_op at 0x7f6709d619e0>, 
  'modifiers', 
  (
    (
      'flags', 
      <BindParameter object at 0x7f670af9fa10>, 
    ),
  ),
  'type', 
  (
    <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes.Boolean'>, 
    (
      'create_constraint', 
      False, 
    ),
  ),
),)
CacheKey(key=(
  '0', 
  <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.BinaryExpression'>, 
  'left', 
  (
    '1', 
    <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.ColumnClause'>, 
    'name', 
    'a', 
    'type', 
    (
      <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes.NullType'>, 
    ),
  ),
  'right', 
  (
    '2', 
    <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.elements.BindParameter'>, 
    (
      <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes.String'>, 
    ),
    '3', 
    False, 
  ),
  'operator', 
  <function regexp_match_op at 0x7f6709d619e0>, 
  'modifiers', 
  (
    (
      'flags', 
      <BindParameter object at 0x7f67099e1910>, 
    ),
  ),
  'type', 
  (
    <class 'sqlalchemy.sql.sqltypes.Boolean'>, 
    (
      'create_constraint', 
      False, 
    ),
  ),

``` 

### Additional context

The interesting part of the output above is the cache key part for the flags parameter of regexp_match:

```
  <function regexp_match_op at 0x7f6709d619e0>, 
  'modifiers', 
  (
    (
      'flags', 
      <BindParameter object at 0x7f67099e1910>, 
    ),
  ),
```

As you can see, it uses the BindParameter object itself instead of its more stable cache key. This results in a different key for every call. I would even argue that a BindParameter object is wrong here, at least for the Postgresql dialect where `flags='i'` results in a different operator being used.
